title: Transition elements
content: Transition elements are elements that have partially filled d subshells (orbitals) which can give rise to cations with incomplete d subshells (orbitals).
e: Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, and their cations can keep an incomplete d subshell. That d-electron pattern is what sets them apart from main-group metals.

title: Complex ion
content: Complex ion is an ion, which has a metal ion at its centre with a number of other molecules or ions surrounding it.
e: A complex ion has a metal ion at the centre with other molecules or ions, called ligands, around it. The ligands surround that central metal ion.

title: Paramagnetic substance
content: Paramagnetic substance is a substance that has unpaired electrons and shows weak attraction towards the external magnetic field.
e: A paramagnetic substance has unpaired electrons, so it is weakly attracted by an external magnetic field. Unpaired electrons are the key.

title: Diamagnetic substance
content: Diamagnetic substance is a substance that has no unpaired electrons and shows no attraction (slight repulsion) from the external magnetic field.
e: A diamagnetic substance has no unpaired electrons. It is not attracted by an external field; it is slightly repelled.

title: Ferromagnetic substance
content: Ferromagnetic substance is a substance that is strongly attracted by the applied magnetic field, and retains its magnetisation for some time even after the external magnetic field is removed.
e: A ferromagnetic substance is strongly attracted by an applied magnetic field and keeps some magnetisation after the field is removed. Iron, cobalt, and nickel behave this way.
